answer.evidence: The tub is an open container. Rows 5-7 are the white back rim and rows 8-11 are the grey inner back wall. Rows 12-20 show blue water with highlights inside the opening, so the contents are seen from above (d). Rows 21-22 are the white front rim, with a grey line at row 23 as the front edge. Rows 23-29 are the vertical front face, drawn as three panels. The top opening spans about rows 5-22 (18 rows) over a 7-row front face. The small item in rows 0-4 is only 9 px wide and sits above the tub, so it counts as decor. The light strip on the right is a vertical rim, not a receding side face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate ofuro is a white/grey tub with a light blue water panel and a small green indicator. Its outline is neutral dark grey, 100% near-neutral dark edge pixels against 0-44% on the material-toned references such as hedge, stall and well. That is the sticker look, not dark material tone. The tub body has only about 3 steps (white, light grey, grey) plus a blue water area. The water and the tub sides are large smooth fills with no grain, no ripples or steam dots, and no per-surface texture. Measured 16% near-flat coverage is above the 0% of hedge and well and the 13% of stall. 11 visible tones per tile is below well (20) and stall (17), though close to hedge (9). By eye the piece looks flatter and thinner than the stall and well, which have shaded stones, planks and tile detail. It is a clean, readable shape but not at the Beodeul standard.
